part_title: Canvas, Ready-to-Use Models and Managed MLflow

scenes.title: SageMaker Canvas
scenes.narration: SageMaker Canvas provides a guided, visual way to create predictions without writing the code for a custom machine learning pipeline. Read the five boxes across the top: import records from S3, clean and transform them in Canvas Data Wrangler, select the prediction target and build a model, inspect metrics and feature insights, then generate predictions on new rows. The lower churn example makes each step concrete. The source table includes customer ID, tenure, monthly charges, contract type and churn. In preprocessing, customer ID is dropped, meaningful numerical and categorical fields are retained, and churn becomes the target label rather than an input. The illustrative feature importance graph ranks contract type highly, and the prediction table shows Yes or No for individual customers. Those are model outputs to evaluate, not certainties about whether a customer will leave. The exam distinction is Canvas for a business analyst who needs a no-code development workflow, versus Studio for a more code-oriented ML environment.

scenes.title: SageMaker Canvas – Ready-to-use models
scenes.narration: The upper flow is shorter than custom model development. Choose an input such as a customer text review, a scanned document or a product photo. In SageMaker Canvas, select an appropriate ready-to-use model, submit the item, and consume its prediction. The three result panels illustrate different tasks: sentiment analysis labels a review positive, negative or neutral; document information extraction returns fields such as a company name, a January fifteenth date, and a two-hundred-forty-five-dollar total; image classification assigns a category such as Shoe. The concrete examples below show a positive shipping review, an invoice number 1042 with extracted date and total, and a white athletic shoe identified as a shoe. These are illustrative successful examples; extracted fields and labels should still be validated where errors carry business consequences. The decision cue is that no custom training is required for these ready-to-use capabilities. Distinguish that from the earlier Canvas workflow, which built a prediction model from the user's own labeled dataset.

scenes.title: MLFlow on Amazon SageMaker
scenes.narration: The architecture runs left to right. A developer uses SageMaker Studio to train and evaluate models. Each run sends parameters, metrics and artifacts to a managed MLflow tracking server on SageMaker AI. Parameters are chosen settings such as learning rate; metrics are measured outcomes such as accuracy; artifacts are saved files, including charts or model outputs. The MLflow Experiments view compares runs and helps select a candidate. The chosen model can then be registered in SageMaker AI Model Registry, where versions and approval states are managed. Examine the lower example: MLflow is configured with a SageMaker tracking-server ARN, and the code logs a learning rate of 0.001, accuracy of 0.92 and a metrics file. The example run table compares 0.92, 0.88 and 0.91 accuracy across different settings. The best numeric score is not automatically an approved deployment: evaluation conditions and business checks still matter. Notice the prerequisites for compatible MLflow packages, the SageMaker integration plugin and IAM permissions. Use this managed integration when experiment tracking and model-version governance are required.
